articles.title: Inflexor Ventures leads Rs 65 Cr investment in Butterfly Learnings to transform paediatric ...
articles.content: August 19, 2026 | Wednesday | News Butterfly Learnings (Bombay Autism Services), India's first full-stack paediatric behavioural health platform for neurodivergent children, has raised Rs 65 crore in its Pre-Series B funding round, led by Inflexor Ventures, with continued participation from existing investors Insitor Partners and Enzia Ventures, reaffirming their conviction in the company's long-term growth. The fresh capital will be used to expand Butterfly's centre network across India, strengthen its technology platform, and commercialise its breakthrough early autism screening solution. Nearly 45 million children across the country are estimated to live with conditions such as Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), ADHD and learning disabilities, yet only a small percentage receive timely intervention. Delayed diagnosis, fragmented care pathways and a shortage of trained specialists continue to prevent children from receiving support during the most critical years of brain development. Mumbai-based startup Butterfly Learnings is the only BHCOE (Behavioural Health Center of Excellence) a ccredited therapist training institute in Asia, reflecting its commitment to globally recognised standards of behavioural healthcare delivery. A key differentiator for Butterfly Learnings is Get SET Early, a patented eye- tracking autism screening technology for which the company holds an exclusive global licence. Following CDSCO approval, the solution enables autism screening in children as young as one year old, helping reduce diagnostic delays and enabling earlier intervention. The newly raised capital will support Butterfly Learnings' expansion from being predominantly focused on Maharashtra to other geographies in India, strengthen its digital and AI capabilities, scale the deployment of Get SET Early through hospitals and pediatricians, and expand its in-house therapist training programme. Looking ahead, Butterfly Learnings plans to deepen its presence across India, strengthen partnerships with hospitals and paediatricians, expand access to inclusive education, advance AI-enabled precision care, reinforcing its mission of making high- quality neurodevelopmental care accessible to families across India.

articles.title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad Bullet Train: India's First High-Speed Rail Corridor Advances With 359 ...
articles.content: Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project is progressing steadily with significant gains recorded across viaducts, track infrastructure, electrification, bridges and tunnels, according to the latest progress update released by National High Speed Rail Corporation Limited (NHSRCL). The NHSRCL is the implementing agency for the 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor, which is the first bullet train project in India. According to the agency's July progress update, pier work has been completed over 453 km and viaduct construction has been undertaken over 359 km. Meanwhile, Reinforced concrete (RC) track bed construction has been completed over 215 km, while 91 km track slabs have been laid with Cement Asphalt Mortar (CAM) injection completed. The electrification infrastructure has also expanded with over 9,000 Overhead Equipment (OHE) masts installed across 200 km of the bullet train corridor, according to the update. These masts will form part of the overhead traction system required to supply power to high-speed trains. Noise barriers have been installed along 297 km of the alignment to reduce the transmission of noise generated during high-speed train operations. A total of 17 river bridges and 15 steel bridges have been completed for the project. Tunnel construction in Maharashtra has also moved ahead. According to the NSHRCL update, four mountain tunnels have been excavated, while 5 km of tunnel constructed using the NATM method has also been completed. The corridor, which is India's first bullet train project, will connect Mumbai and Ahmedabad through 12 stations across Maharashtra, Gujarat and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw had earlier announced that India’s first bullet train will begin its inaugural 100-km run between Surat and Vapi in August 2027, The New Indian Express reported . The section is part of the larger 508-km Mumbai–Ahmedabad high-speed corridor, also known as Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project, which is expected to be fully operational by 2029. Vaishnaw said the Mumbai–Ahmedabad travel time would drop to 1 hour 58 minutes once the corridor is ready. He added that the first operational run in August 2027 would be limited to the 100-km Surat–Vapi stretch. "A significant milestone is that the bullet train will cover the distance between Ahmedabad and Mumbai in just 1 hour 58 minutes upon the completion of the high-speed rail corridor. The inaugural run in August 2027 will cover 100 km between Surat and Vapi," Vaishaw said. The minister said trains on the 508-km corridor will operate at speeds of up to 320 kmph. With four stops, the Mumbai–Ahmedabad trip will take 1 hour 58 minutes, while halting at all 12 stations will extend the journey to 2 hours 17 minutes. "The bullet train will cover the distance between Mumbai and Ahmedabad in 1 hour 58 minutes with four stops. However, if it halts at all 12 stations, the total journey time will be 2 hours 17 minutes,” Vaishnaw said. The corridor will be opened in phases, covering the Vapi-Surat, Vapi-Ahmedabad, and Thane-Ahmedabad stretc h es before the Mumbai-Ahmedabad section becomes operational in the final stage. articles.title: India's FIRST 14-metre acoustic-transparent 4K LED cinema screen opens in Kochi
articles.content: India’s FIRST 14-metre acoustic-transparent 4K LED cinema screen opens in Kochi Edited By: Riya Ashok Madayi India's first 14-metre acoustic-transparent Direct View 4K HDR LED cinema screen was unveiled at Magic Frames in Kakkanad, Kochi. Photo | Special Arrangement A new cinema screen in Kochi is bringing a technology not previously installed at this scale in India. Magic Frames in Kakkanad has unveiled a 14-metre acoustic-transparent Direct View 4K HDR LED cinema screen, making it the first installation of its kind in the country. The screen is part of MAGNOVA, a premium large-format cinema offering from UFO Cinema Solutions, powered by HEYLED technology. The installation measures 14 metres by 6 metres and uses a DCI-compliant Direct View LED display with 4K HDR capability and a 3.91 mm pixel pitch. Unlike a conventional projection setup, where an image is projected onto a screen, a Direct View LED system produces the image directly through the display itself. What makes the screen different? The key technology behind the Kochi installation is its acoustic-transparent architecture. ALSO READ: Nivin Pauly's 'Bethlehem Kudumba Unit': Malayalam cinema's ultimate onam package? In a conventional LED cinema screen, placing speakers directly behind the display can be a challenge because the screen itself can obstruct the path of sound. The MAGNOVA installation has been designed to allow cinema speakers to be positioned behind the 14-metre-wide LED display. This means the audio can originate from behind the image, aligning the source of the sound with what appears on screen. The setup is paired with Dolby Atmos immersive audio and Pulz Cinema Speakers. The acoustic-transparent architecture allows cinema speakers to be positioned behind the LED display. Photo | Special Arrangement The display also offers 4K HDR presentation, along with the characteristics associated with Direct View LED technology, including high brightness, contrast and the absence of projector-based light spill. The technical specifications at a glance- The MAGNOVA screen installed in Kochi features: Screen size: 14 metres x 6 metres Display technology: Direct View LED Resolution: 4K HDR: Yes Compliance: DCI-compliant Pixel pitch: 3.91 mm Technology: Powered by HEYLED Audio setup: Dolby Atmos Speakers: Pulz Cinema Speakers Key feature: Acoustic-transparent LED architecture allowing speakers to be placed behind the screen The installation represents a different approach to theatrical presentation, combining a large-format LED display with an audio configuration designed around speaker placement behind the image. From projection to Direct View LED Cinema technology has moved through several display formats, from film projection to digital projection, while Direct View LED has emerged as another option for theatrical exhibition. The 14m x 6m MAGNOVA display uses Direct View 4K HDR LED technology with a 3.91mm pixel pitch. Photo | Special Arrangement With a Direct View LED system, the display itself produces the image instead of relying on a projector and reflected light. The Kochi installation combines this display technology with an acoustic-transparent design, addressing the placement of speakers behind a large LED cinema screen. articles.title: Bengaluru To Host India's First Happiness Summit - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Cities Bangalore Bengaluru To Host India’s First Happiness Summit Bangalore Urban news Bengaluru To Host India’s First Happiness Summit By UrbanPost August 19, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bengaluru To Host India’s First Happiness Summit Bengaluru is set to host India’s first World Happiness Summit, bringing policymakers, researchers, business leaders and wellbeing practitioners together to examine how quality of life can become a more measurable part of development. The event is expected to place issues such as mental wellbeing, social connection and inclusive growth alongside conventional indicators of economic progress. The summit comes as Indian cities face a growing gap between economic expansion and everyday liveability. Bengaluru remains one of the country’s strongest technology and employment centres, but rapid growth has also intensified pressure on housing, transport, public spaces and basic urban services. These factors directly shape how residents experience the city. The concept of urban wellbeing extends beyond individual happiness. Access to safe streets, affordable housing, reliable public transport, clean air, green spaces and essential services can influence physical and emotional quality of life. For a rapidly expanding city, these factors are closely linked to whether economic growth remains inclusive. Bengaluru provides a particularly relevant setting for that discussion. Its large technology workforce and expanding business districts have generated employment and investment, while long commuting times, traffic congestion and rising living costs have become persistent concerns for many residents. A city can therefore perform strongly in economic indicators while producing uneven experiences of urban life. Urban planners increasingly use broader measures of liveability when assessing development. Public spaces, walkability, access to nature and social infrastructure can affect how residents interact with their neighbourhoods. These considerations are also relevant to climate resilience, as trees, shaded streets and well-designed public areas can reduce heat exposure while improving everyday comfort. The summit’s value will ultimately depend on whether discussions translate into measurable approaches that cities can use. Wellbeing indicators could potentially complement conventional measures such as investment, employment and infrastructure delivery, giving policymakers a clearer picture of whether growth is improving everyday life. There is also an economic case for this approach. Cities that provide healthier and more accessible environments can improve workforce productivity, attract talent and strengthen social cohesion. Businesses increasingly consider quality of life when employees choose where to live and work, making urban wellbeing part of the wider competitiveness equation. For Bengaluru, the event offers an opportunity to connect its economic ambitions with the lived experience of residents. The challenge will be moving the conversation beyond the language of happiness and towards practical improvements in housing, mobility, public spaces, environmental quality and access to services. If those links are made effectively, the summit could contribute to a broader understanding of urban success—one in which a city’s progress is judged not only by its economic output, but also by how safely, affordably and comfortably people can live within it. articles.title: Razorpay unveils Vulcan AI model to boost India's digital payments - TechGig
articles.content: AI 2 min read Razorpay unveils Vulcan AI model to boost India's digital payments Razorpay has launched Vulcan, India's first Transformer-based AI Foundation Model for payments, designed to enhance the reliability and security of digital transactions. This new model aims to address common payment frictions like failed transactions and fraud, which often deter first-time digital users. TechGig Published On Aug 18, 2026 at 10:53 AM IST Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Highlights Razorpay launched Vulcan, India's first Transformer-based AI Foundation Model for payments. Built with NVIDIA and AWS, Vulcan aims to enhance payment reliability, safety, and predictability. Early results show 8-10% higher payment success rates and 8x more international card fraud detected. The model learns from 3 trillion data points across 4 billion payments, understanding money movement. Razorpay , India 's Omnichannel Payments Platform for Businesses, has introduced Vulcan, the country's first Transformer-based AI Foundation Model specifically built for payments. Developed in collaboration with NVIDIA and AWS , Vulcan leverages Razorpay's extensive payments data, NVIDIA's accelerated computing, and AWS's cloud infrastructure to create a more reliable, safer, and predictable digital payment experience across India. An internal Razorpay study involving 1.5 million shoppers and over 51,000 businesses revealed consistent payment friction, including failed transactions, drop-offs, and delays, impacting users from metropolitan areas to small towns. This finding underscored the need for a unified solution rather than fragmented models. Advt Early Impact and Capabilities Prior to its full launch, components of the Razorpay Foundation Model were tested on 3 trillion data points within the company's network, influencing routing, fraud, and risk decisions on live transactions. Early adopters, including Blinkit, Bachatt, and redBus, have reported significant benefits. The model has demonstrated an 8-10% improvement in payment success rates and an 8x increase in the detection of international card fraud. It also identifies 5x more fraudulent or disputed transactions without escalating alert volumes. Additionally, 40% more shoppers are seeing their preferred UPI app on Razorpay Magic Checkout, contributing to 1-2 lakh more purchases monthly. Technical Foundation Vulcan is a proprietary, ground-up model trained on approximately 3 trillion data points across 4 billion payments, learning from roughly 3,000 signals per transaction. Unlike traditional machine learning models that address specific problems, this foundation model understands the intricate movement of money across the entire payments ecosystem, extending its learning to new use cases without requiring retraining. While drawing architectural inspiration from Transformer technology used in large language models (LLMs), Vulcan is specifically adapted to understand the "language" of money movement rather than text. Advt Harshil Mathur, CEO & Founder of Razorpay, emphasised the model's role in building trust among Indian digital payment users. "Every payment teaches the system something that makes the next payment better. That's what makes this feel less like a product launch, and more like the starting point for how payments in India keep getting better on their own, for years to come," Mathur said. articles.title: Samsung Solve for Tomorrow Names India's Top 40 Young Innovators
articles.content: Technology For SMEs News Samsung Solve for Tomorrow Names India’s Top 40 Young Innovators The Top 40 represent 15 states and 26 cities, with more than half of the teams coming from Tier 2 and Tier 3 India. Young innovators from Varanasi, Coimbatore, Guntur, Amritsar, Sundargarh and Rajkot have made it to the national semi-finals alongside teams from major technology and education hubs. SMEStreet Edit Desk 18 Aug 2026 10:50 IST Follow Us New Update Listen to this article 0.75x 1x 1.5x 00:00 / 00:00 Samsung India announced the Top 40 semi-finalist teams of Samsung Solve for Tomorrow, its flagship youth innovation programme that gives young people a platform to identify challenges around them and turn their ideas into solutions through mentorship, technology, prototyping and hands-on learning. Now in its fifth edition in India in 2026, Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is open to young people aged 14 to 22 and is designed to nurture problem-solving and innovation among the country’s next generation. The Top 40 represent 15 states and 26 cities, with more than half of the teams coming from Tier 2 and Tier 3 India. Young innovators from Varanasi, Coimbatore, Guntur, Amritsar, Sundargarh and Rajkot have made it to the national semi-finals alongside teams from major technology and education hubs. The shortlist comprises 10 teams each across the four themes of Samsung Solve for Tomorrow 2026 – AI Living for India, Health and Education, Environmental Sustainability, and Sport & Tech. “What stands out in this year’s Top 40 is how closely young people are looking at the world around them. They are identifying problems in their communities, classrooms, farms, businesses and playing fields, and asking how technology can make a difference. The fact that more than half of these teams come from Tier 2 and Tier 3 India is particularly encouraging because it shows that the next generation of innovation can emerge from anywhere. Our role through Samsung Solve for Tomorrow is to give these young innovators the mentorship, technology and opportunity to turn their ambition into impact. As Samsung completes 30 years in India, we want to continue investing in the ideas and talent that will shape the country’s next 30 years,” said SP Chun, Corporate Vice President, Samsung Southwest Asia. The semi-finalists are working on ideas ranging from AI tools that could make financial and essential information more accessible to solutions for agricultural residue, assistive technologies for people with disabilities, affordable healthcare and education tools, and technologies designed to make sport more inclusive. Among the Top 40 is AIRMED from Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, which is exploring how AI could help built about India as a global healthcare destination. AIRMED wants to connect overseas patients with Indian hospitals. Code Blooded from Sundargarh, Odisha uses specialised AI to identify sporting talent among para-athletes in smaller cities and rural areas. AcoustiNode Systems from Thrissur, Kerala addresses dam management through better hydrological intelligence, with the aim of reducing poorly informed reservoir releases and improving flood, irrigation and power-management decisions.
